task: Fix the deadlock in the order fulfillment pipeline after the inventory lock refactor.

candidate_memories.content: Deadlock traces show fulfillment goroutines acquiring inventory lock then order lock; previous code did the reverse.
Lock acquisition order must be: order lock → inventory lock → shipment lock across all fulfillment code paths.
The inventory lock refactor in sprint 14 reversed the lock order in two out of five code paths.
When a deadlock is introduced by a refactor, audit all lock acquisitions before fixing any single path.
The deadlock only manifests when more than 200 concurrent orders are in flight; single-order tests pass.
The order fulfillment service was split from the monolith in 2021.
The order dashboard pagination was fixed in session 6 to handle large result sets.
Old lesson: use per-resource locks rather than global locks for inventory management.
Inventory data is synced from the ERP system every 15 minutes.
Session 10 note: the fulfillment team requested a bulk cancel feature.
Old inventory guide: shipment lock was acquired first before the inventory refactor.
A performance test in session 13 showed the order API handles 500 rps at p99 120ms.
The shipment tracking integration uses a third-party webhook from FedEx.
Old practice: single global mutex was used for all inventory operations before the refactor.
The order fulfillment dashboard was redesigned with Gantt chart view in session 4.
Fulfillment workers run as Kubernetes Jobs with a 15-minute timeout.
Session 7 note: email notifications for order status were added.
The ERP sync produces an audit log of all inventory changes.
In distributed systems, use consistent lock ordering across all code paths to prevent deadlocks.
Old fulfillment guide: the fulfillment SLA was 24 hours before it was tightened to 4 hours.
